title: Incident bot: add “suspected change” heuristic for deploy/config overlap near degradation start
author: Jacob Stein
description:
Motivation: During early triage we repeatedly ask “what changed right before this started?” even when the bot already posts deploys + config diffs. This PR adds a lightweight heuristic to highlight deploy/config deltas that temporally overlap the start of the degradation window, without implying causality. The output is intentionally conservative (guardrails + disclaimers) to avoid the bot overclaiming root cause. Approach: 1) Determine a degradation start timestamp (t0). For now we use incident.created_at as the primary anchor; if alert payload includes a `degradation_start_ts` (from paging/alert metadata) we prefer that. If neither is present we do not compute suspected changes and show a short “insufficient timing signal” note. 2) Define a suspicion window around t0: default [-20m, +10m]. (Configurable via `SUSPECTED_CHANGE_WINDOW_MINUTES` but clamped to max 45m total to avoid noisy correlation.) 3) Pull candidates from existing collectors: a) Deploy collector: deploy events already collected per service + region; filter to those with `finished_at` within the suspicion window. b) Config diff collector: effective config snapshot diff already computed between t-30m and now; additionally we compute per-key “changed_at” when audit metadata is present (event-sourced snapshot) and only mark keys as “overlapping” when the change timestamp falls in window. If change timestamp is missing, we mark as “timing unknown” and do NOT include in suspected list (guardrail). 4) Score candidates and render: score is a simple weighted sum (region match + closeness to t0 + rollout stage/canary). We then render up to 3 items. If more exist we show “+N more (see deploy/config sections)”. Output copy uses “Suspected change (timing overlap)” language and includes “Correlation only” disclaimer. Guardrails / safety: - Never claim causality (“caused by”, “root cause”). - Do not include config keys that are not already allowlisted for safe posting; suspected-change uses the same `safe_to_post` classification output from config diff collector. - Only show config changes when we have an explicit change timestamp; otherwise omit from suspected list (still present in full config diff section). - If the incident is in restricted mode, suspected-change renders only service/region + “recent change overlap detected (restricted)” and pushes the details to the restricted channel bundle. - If collectors are missing/errored, suspected-change block is omitted entirely (no partial guesses). Example Slack rendering (new block appears after “Summary” and before collectors): "Suspected changes (timing overlap; correlation only)
• deploy: router-api@v2.18.4 (us-east-1) finished 2m before degradation (canary 25%) → GitHub PR / pipeline
• config: routing.policy.max_inflight (us-east-1) changed 6m after degradation → change event
See full details below." Testing: - Unit tests covering windowing + sorting + clamping + “no t0” behavior. - Fixture-based integration tests using recorded deploy events + config audit metadata (with a negative test ensuring missing change timestamps are excluded). Follow-ups: - Improve t0 determination by pulling “first sustained SLO burn start” from telemetry once we have a stable query endpoint (tracked in ENG-2845 notes). - Consider showing model-level suspected changes once saturation collector is always present (but only if we can avoid cardinality/noise).
